amendments.because: The owner decided on 2026-10-01 that tests don't count toward the five-file fix limit, after most allowances that day were for tests changing with the code
amendments.done_when: The fix-size limit (the commit hook and close) doesn't count files whose content is exactly what forge sync writes for this repo; any other change to them, and every other file, still counts. A command-level test commits an upgrade fix whose only code changes are forge sync's output (accepted without an allowance) and one that also edits a synced file by hand beyond sync's output (counted).

done_when: The fix-size limit (the commit hook and close) counts only non-test code files: it doesn't count test files (the repo's test paths Forge already recognises) or files whose content is exactly what forge sync writes for this repo; any other change to a synced file, and every other code file, still counts, and the interface rule is unchanged. Command-level tests: an upgrade fix whose only code changes are forge sync's output closes without an allowance; one that also hand-edits a synced file is counted; a fix with four source files and three test files commits without an allowance.

findings.body: The sync comparison receives the current checkout's forge.toml, although it examines the pushed SHA. A fix that changes models.build.effort and runs forge sync changes five Codex build-role files (src/forge/roles.py:32–43, 83–91). Committing inside that fix succeeds, but pushing it from the main checkout with `git push origin fix/<name>` compares those files against main's old settings and incorrectly counts all five plus forge.toml, refusing the push without an allowance. Uncommitted configuration edits can cause the same mismatch. Read the pushed commit's configuration for the sync comparison while retaining the existing interface-rule configuration.
findings.title: Use the pushed commit's config to recognise sync output

why: An upgrade fix can't commit without the owner's allowance because forge sync's own output (host hooks, skills and eleven subagent roles per tool) counts toward the five-code-file fix limit
